company_items.summary: AutoZone reported FQ4 EPS of $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — 145 basis points of gross margin tailwind came from tariff refunds and another 105 basis points from a non-cash LIFO impact. Domestic comps disappointed at +1.6% vs. the +3.1% expected, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex more aggressively in the physical AI and robotics space.

MillerKnoll beat FQ1 EPS estimates handily at 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and critically the beat holds even excluding the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind — adjusted EPS of 42 cents still topped consensus. Sales fell short, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. $943.2 million expected, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed slightly, but the EPS range was left unchanged and FQ2 EPS guidance is in line with consensus.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings significant large-cap CFO experience, having previously held the role at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS estimates at 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% versus the 13.85% expected — management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and rising material costs pressuring household budgets and retail demand. Revenue came in at $2.311 billion, slightly above the $2.17 billion estimate but still down 8.4% year-over-year. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost-reduction actions underway, and a ~75% surge in North American towable RV order backlog.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in participants. The data represents a meaningful milestone in a highly competitive obesity drug market. The strong trial readout positions VK2735 as a credible competitor in the GLP-1 space.

tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday September 22nd, so there is no broad macro or rates commentary today — let's go straight to the names moving before the open.

Starting with AutoZone. The company beat fourth-quarter earnings at $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the quality of that beat is a real concern. About 145 basis points of gross margin help came from tariff refunds, and another 105 basis points from a non-cash LIFO adjustment. Strip those out and the picture gets murkier. Domestic comps were only up 1.6% against expectations of 3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management was constructive on sales trends improving in the back half of the quarter and said they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027 growth, but this is a mixed print at best.

MillerKnoll was a cleaner story. First-quarter EPS came in at 53 cents versus 36 cents expected, and importantly, even backing out the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, they still would have beaten at 42 cents. Sales missed slightly, down 3.3% organically, but orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year EPS guidance was left unchanged and the second-quarter midpoint is in line with consensus. That's a solid result.

On THOR Industries — this one disappointed. Fourth-quarter EPS of 78 cents missed the 87-cent estimate, gross margins fell 230 basis points to 12.4% against expectations of nearly 14%, and management's tone was cautious, pointing to stubborn interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation squeezing household budgets. That said, dealer inventory is healthy, structural cost actions are underway, and North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year — so there are real pockets of optimism buried in an otherwise soft print.

Cognex is making a significant move, acquiring RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and physical AI — for roughly $500 million upfront plus another $106 million. RealSense is growing revenue more than 50% year-over-year in the $80 to $90 million range. This is a bold bet on the robotics and physical AI buildout and the market will likely view it as strategically sound.

Finally, Viking Therapeutics is the standout mover today. Shares are spiking pre-market after the company reported 22% weight loss results from its GLP-1 drug VK2735 trial. In a space where Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk dominate, a 22% weight loss figure is a serious data point that puts Viking firmly on the map as a competitive threat.

The session today is event-driven with no macro catalyst on the calendar — focus will be on how these prints trade off the open. Viking and MillerKnoll are the cleanest bullish setups; AutoZone's beat-on-paper but miss-on-quality is the one to watch for a potential fade.
